strategies.title: Explicit formula and prime-counting consequences
strategies.approach: Examine whether a precise explicit-formula route can connect zero locations to a quantitative statement about prime counting. State the exact implication being targeted, list analytic hypotheses and smoothing/error terms, and attempt to prove one bounded lemma. Test whether the argument actually forces every zero onto the critical line or only gives weaker density or error information. No numerical data or references may be invented.

strategies.title: Spectral realization with operator obligations
strategies.approach: Investigate a spectral route in which imaginary parts of zeros would arise from spectral data. Replace analogy with a concrete operator, domain, inner product, and proposed trace relation. The central obligations are self-adjointness, correspondence in both directions, and exact treatment of multiplicity and trivial zeros. If no operator satisfying them can be constructed, record the obstruction rather than treating a formal analogy as progress.

strategies.title: Zero-free region and density estimates
strategies.approach: Seek a rigorous partial theorem that narrows where zeros may lie or bounds their density, then identify the precise gap between that result and the Riemann Hypothesis. Make every estimate's range and constants explicit. Challenge extrapolations from finite computations and distinguish a zero-free region near Re(s)=1 from a proof on the full critical strip.
